title: A Hyena Bites With 1,100 PSI to Crack Bones Other Animals Can't

scenes.text: A hyena's bite is built to crack bone.
Spotted hyenas bite with about eleven hundred pounds per square inch.
That's roughly forty percent more pressure than a leopard.
Huge jaw muscles and a short snout put the force right at the hinge.
Even the skull is built for it. A hollow, vaulted forehead spreads the stress.
They eat whole skeletons, and even the marrow inside the bones.

description:
Spotted hyenas have a bite force of about 1,100 psi, built for cracking bones.
Their skull has a special sinus that spreads the stress.
Would you want to meet one?
first_comment: Which bite would you fear more: hyena or crocodile?
